findings.title: Device limit can be bypassed because cache is set before persistence
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, the device key is inserted into `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs. When the configured device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which makes `Anonymous.Authenticate` fail for that request; however, the cache entry remains. A retry with the same device ID hits the cache at line 83 and returns nil without checking the store, so authentication then succeeds and the limit is bypassed for the cache TTL (29 minutes). Move `SetDefault` after a successful store, or remove the cache entry on error.

findings.title: Device count check and insert are not atomic, so limit can be exceeded under concurrency
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` first calls `CountDevices` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, proceeds to the INSERT/upsert. The count and insert are separate statements with no transaction or lock preventing concurrent inserts. When multiple new anonymous devices arrive while the count is just below the limit, several goroutines can all observe `count < deviceLimit` and insert, exceeding the configured `device_limit`. The limit should be enforced atomically, for example with a transaction, row lock, or an `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(...)) < ?` approach.

findings.title: Anonymous device tagging is now synchronous even when device limit is disabled
findings.body: The previous implementation tagged devices in a background goroutine with a timeout. This PR moves `TagDevice` into the authentication path unconditionally. With the default `AnonymousDeviceLimit = 0`, no limit enforcement is needed, but every uncached anonymous request still synchronously performs the DB write/upsert before authentication can complete. This adds latency and database load to anonymous/public dashboard traffic for installations that did not enable the new limit. Consider keeping the old asynchronous path when `deviceLimit <= 0` or gating synchronous enforcement behind `deviceLimit > 0`.
